name: OH-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Bob Latta running with large financial edge
model.rationale: Latta is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by twelve points, while Shaver has raised almost nothing and no polls or expert ratings suggest competitiveness. Markets price a Republican win at 94%, consistent with a double-digit margin.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would be the main reason to revisit this.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Ohio's fifth district is solidly Republican territory, and Bob Latta has held the seat since 2007. He enters the general election with about $1 million on hand after raising nearly $1.5 million, while Democratic challenger Brian Shaver has raised under $12,000 and has minimal cash. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets give Latta roughly a 94% chance of winning. The district's partisan lean and the lopsided fundraising gap point to a comfortable Republican win in the mid-teens, with limited evidence of any competitive dynamic developing.
